back: z = (x − mean) / standard deviation. It says how many standard deviations a value is from the mean.

front: Why is the plain z-score weak against big outliers?
back: The outlier inflates the mean and the standard deviation, so its own z-score becomes smaller (masking).
0.6745 · (x − median) / MAD. Median and MAD are not changed much by outliers. Typical cut-off: 3.5.
Median absolute deviation: the median of |x − median|. A robust measure of spread.

front: How do you avoid leakage in a rolling z-score?
back: Score x(t) using only values before t. In pandas: shift(1) before rolling. Never put x(t) in its own window.
